title.narrative: Specialised Link and Learn Grantee C2

description.narrative:
Overall Objective: To strengthen structured peer learning, coordinated youth advocacy, and cross-continental collaboration among Cohort 2 Youth Action Lab grantees by organizing an innovative Annual Link <(>&<)> Learn Event in Kenya and coordinating youth-led influencing linked to African Union, European Union, and United Nations policy fora between May 2026 and April 2027.
RESULT AREA 1: Organizing and Facilitating the Annual Link <(>&<)> Learn Event (8–10 December 2026, Nairobi, Kenya). Strategic Linkage: The event will culminate on 10 December 2026 – International Human Rights Day, positioning youth-led solutions within global human rights discourse and ensuring international advocacy relevance.
Phase 1: Co-Creation <(>&<)> Thematic Development (May – July 2026) Objective: Toco-create a learning framework that reflects the needs of Cohort 2 grantees and builds on previous Link <(>&<)> Learn outcomes. Activities: May 2026: Launch digital needs assessment survey to all Cohort 2 grantees. Review 2025 Link <(>&<)> Learn outcomes and documented lessons. Mapping of thematic priorities emerging from Entrepreneurship, Innovation, Representation, and Cooperation grants June 2026: Virtual co-creation workshop with Youth Advisory Board, Joint planning meeting with Consortium Partners, Thematic validation call with Digital Online Grantee July 2026: Finalization of Learning Theme, Definition of learning objectives and measurable outcomes, Development of event concept note and agenda framework Proposed Theme:“Scaling Youth-Led Solutions for Human Rights, Economic Justice and Inclusive Governance” Deliverable: Co-Created Learning Framework Document (July 2026)
Phase 2: Strategic Influencing Alignment Before Event (June – August 2026). To ensure chronological coherence and strategic positioning June 2026: European Development Days: Youth Action Lab visibility campaign highlighting Cohort 2 solutions. Deliverable: Digital youth solutions spotlight campaign aligned with EU development priorities. 12 August 2026: International Youth Day: Coordinated social media campaign with Digital Online Grantee. Deliverables: Joint messaging toolkit, Youth testimonial series, Digital advocacy graphics
Phase 3: Logistics <(>&<)>Procurement (August – October 2026). Objective: To ensure compliant, safe, and efficient delivery of a 100-participant convening. Activities: August 2026: Venue procurement in Nairobi, Safeguarding and accessibility compliance checks, Budget finalization for conference services September 2026, Registration launch, Invitation letters issued, Visa support coordination, Flight and accommodation coordination support to grantees October 2026: Payment of conference facilities, Booking and payment of logistics for 7 Consortium Partner staff(flights, visa, 7 nights accommodation, per diem), Booking of accommodation for 2 additional consortium partners (2 extra nights) Airport transfer contracts secured, Procurement of conference materials (tote bags, notebooks, badges, banners) Deliverable:Confirmed logistics plan and participant pack (October 2026)
Phase 4: Annual Link <(>&<)> Learn Event (8–10 December 2026) Day 1 – Linking <(>&<)> Showcasing: Innovation Marketplace (booth exhibitions of youth solutions), Structured “Solution Speed Networking”,Regional cluster dialogues Day 2 – Capacity Strengthening, World Café cross-thematic exchanges, Hybrid dialogue with AU, EU, UN youth focal points, Advocacy Labs (co-design of unified messaging), Policy Simulation Exercise (mock AU/EU negotiation format) Day 3 – Influencing <(>&<)> Outputs, Drafting of Youth Advocacy Statement, Action Planning Session, Media Roundtable, Formal adoption of Advocacy Statement on 10 December 2026 Deliverables (December 2026), 3-day Annual Link <(>&<)> Learn Event (±100 participants), Youth Advocacy Statement and Policy Brief, Action Plan, Press Statement, Event Documentation Report
RESULT AREA 2 Coordinated Influencing Linked to Regional and International Fora (January – April 2027) January 2027: Dissemination of Link <(>&<)> Learn Report, Distribution of Advocacy Statement to AU, EU, and UN youth desks, Development of Unified Messaging Toolkit, Monthly coordination calls with Digital Online Grantee begin Deliverable: Advocacy Dissemination Package February 2027 – African Union Summit Relevance:Platform for engagement with AU Heads of State and policy organs. Action: Submission of Youth Advocacy Statement to AU Youth Envoy Office, Engagement with ECOSOCC youth structures, Circulation of recommendations linked to youth governance and economic justice Deliverable: AU Advocacy Brief Submission
African Youth Charter Review <(>&<)> Amendment Advocacy The African Youth Charter, adopted in 2006, marks over 20 years of existence and requires review to reflect contemporary youth realities including digital rights, green transitions, migration, and economic justice. Action (February–March 2027): Extract Charter-relevant recommendations from Link <(>&<)> Learn outcomes, Develop Policy Brief on Youth Recommendations for Charter Amendment, Share brief with AU Department of Health, Humanitarian Affairs <(>&<)> Social Development, Facilitate virtual consultation with youth grantees to validate recommendations Deliverable: YouthPosition Paper on African Youth Charter Review March 2027 – UN Human Rights Council Session Relevance: Global human rights policy forum. Action: Circulate Youth Advocacy Statement through civil society networks, Promote youth human rights framing of Link <(>&<)> Learn outcomes
March 2027 – Commission on the Status of Women Action: Highlight gender equality solutionsfrom Cohort 2 grantees, Coordinate digital spotlight series April 2027: Consolidated influencing report, Final dissemination campaign, Participation in YAL Grant Management meetings, Submission of final narrative and financial reports Final DeliverablesSummary: Annual Link <(>&<)> Learn Event, Youth Advocacy Statement, Learning Event Report, Press Statement, Action Plan, African Youth Charter Amendment Policy Brief, AU, EU, UN dissemination outputs, Unified Messaging Toolkit, Narrative <(>&<)> Financial Report

participating-org.narrative:
Youth Senate Kenya (YSK) is a nationally registered, youth-led non-profit organization advancing meaningful youth participation in governance, public policy processes, economic empowerment, social accountability, and global development discourse. YSK champions a youth-led development model that strengthens democratic dialogue by creating structured platforms for engagement between young people and decision-makers at county, national, regional,and international levels, ensuring active and informed participation in governance processes.
YSK’s mission is to strengthen youth leadership, institutional accountability, and inclusive policymaking by buildingthe capacity of emerging young leaders and facilitating sustained dialogue between youth constituencies and public institutions. Its vision is a society where young people meaningfully influence governance systems, development priorities, and global agendas through structured, solution-driven engagement.
The organization operates nationally in Kenya and regionally across Africa as part of the African Youth Commission, YSK partners with actors aligned with African Union and multilateral youth processes. The organization convenes high-level policy dialogues, youth forums, regional consultations, and thematic working groups, while producing policy briefs,advocacy statements, and youth-informed recommendations that shape public discourse.
Guided by the core values of inclusion, accountability, youth ownership, innovation, collaboration, and integrity, YSK integrates digital engagement with in-person convenings to amplify youth voices and connect grassroots realities to continental and global policy spaces.
